steps.body: The same quotient can be reported two ways. 13 ÷ 4 is 3 remainder 1, or 3 1/4 — and which is right depends on whether the leftover can be cut.
steps.narration: The same quotient can be reported two ways. 13 ÷ 4 is 3 remainder 1, or 3 1/4 — and which is right depends on whether the leftover can be cut.

widget.prompt: 13 ÷ 4 as a mixed number: build the FRACTION part.
widget.successFeedback: 1/4 — three whole sandwiches each, plus a quarter from the one left over.
widget.lowFeedback: That build is SHORTER than 1/4 — either shade more pieces or make each piece larger until the lengths match.
widget.highFeedback: That build is LONGER than 1/4 — either shade fewer pieces or make each piece smaller until the lengths match.

commonFractions.feedback: 3/4 is what 3 ÷ 4 gives; here the leftover is a single sandwich shared four ways.
Thirds appear nowhere — the sandwich is shared among four people.

predict.prompt: 13 people into 4-seat cars — fraction or remainder?
predict.reveal: A quarter of a person is meaningless, so the leftover stays whole and needs another car.

cml.actionGoal: Ask what is being cut and how big each piece is, then count the pieces for g5fd interpret.
invariants: Division and fractions are the same act seen twice: sharing a wholes among b people gives a/b, and dividing BY a piece asks how many of it fit, which is why g5fd interpret produces a larger answer when the divisor is under one.
misconceptions: Reading "divide by 1/4" as "take a quarter of", reporting a remainder when the leftover could be shared, or shrinking the pieces when only their count should change.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the divisor grew past one, would the answer become larger or smaller than the dividend?

widget.prompt: 13 ÷ 4 gives 3 remainder 1. When is the answer 3 1/4 rather than "3 remainder 1"?

options.label: When the leftover can be shared equally
options.feedback: Correct — a divisible leftover becomes a fraction; an indivisible one, like people, stays a remainder.

options.label: Always — remainders are never correct
options.feedback: Remainders are right when the objects cannot be split, such as buses or whole people.

options.label: Never — 3 1/4 is a different answer
options.feedback: They describe the same division; which form is right depends on what is being shared.

options.label: Only when the divisor is 4
options.feedback: The divisor's size is irrelevant; what matters is whether the leftover can be cut.

hints: If so, it is a fraction.

The leftover 1 thirds fall short of the 3 needed for another whole.
